verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is a marketing claim that Fly Machines boot in under a second and "scale out to tens of thousands when the traffic arrives." That implies traffic-driven scale-out, but nothing documents a load-based autoscaling mechanism, its triggers, or its configuration. The `fly scale` command is manual scaling, so it is adjacent and gets no credit toward automatic autoscaling. Missing for 10: documented load/metric-based autoscaling configuration (thresholds, min/max, concurrency triggers), confirmation that scale-out is automatic rather than operator-driven, and independent or hands-on corroboration of absorbing bursts.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can rely on load-based autoscaling to absorb large traffic bursts automatically

citations.quote: Fly Machines are hardware-isolated VMs that boot in under a second, run close to your users, and scale out to tens of thousands when the traffic arrives.
